title: Show HN: Remoroo - Fixing Memory in Long-Running Coding Agents
description: Remoroo is a project showcased on Hacker News that attempts to fix memory issues in long-running coding agents. This highlights ongoing challenges with agent memory and context management.
author: adhamghazali

title: Graphs That Explain the State of AI in 2026
description: IEEE article with graphs explaining the state of AI in 2026, featured on Hacker News. Provides data-driven insights into AI developments and trends.
author: bryanrasmussen

title: Opus 4.7 to 4.6 Inflation is ~45%
description: Hacker News discussion about token inflation between Claude Opus 4.7 and 4.6 models, measuring approximately 45%. This highlights changing token economics in LLMs.
author: billchambers.me

title: Measuring Claude 4.7's Tokenizer Costs
description: Popular Hacker News post analyzing Claude 4.7's tokenizer costs with 677 points and 472 comments. Shows strong community interest in understanding LLM token economics.
author: aray07

title: I'm Spending Months Coding the Old Way
description: Miguel Connor's Substack post featured on Hacker News about spending months coding without AI assistance. Generated 317 points and 305 comments, showing community debate about AI's role in coding.
author: miguelconner.substack.com

title: LLM Knowledge Bases - Andrej Karpathy's New Workflow
description: Karpathy shared a new workflow using LLMs to build personal knowledge bases for research topics. An 'LLM Wiki' pattern where AI agents compile living, evolving markdown libraries rather than traditional RAG retrieval. Works with tools like Obsidian for markdown-based knowledge management.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Anthropic launches Claude Design for Quick Visuals
description: Anthropic launched Claude Design, a new product for creating quick visuals. This is Anthropic's entry into the AI design space, competing with tools like Midjourney and DALL-E.
author: Aisha Malik

title: 'Tokenmaxxing' is Making Developers Less Productive
description: Tim Fernholz explores how 'tokenmaxxing' - the practice of maximizing LLM usage - may be making developers less productive than they think. The article questions whether excessive AI assistance is actually harming productivity.
author: Tim Fernholz

title: Cursor in Talks to Raise $2B+ at $50B Valuation
description: AI coding assistant Cursor is in talks to raise over $2B at a $50B valuation as enterprise growth surges. This reflects the massive growth and investment in AI-powered coding tools.
author: Marina Temkin

title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on my laptop drew me a better pelican than Claude Opus 4.7
description: Comparison between Alibaba's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 models using Simon's 'pelican riding a bicycle' benchmark. Local open source model is competitive with top-tier proprietary models.
author: Simon Willison

title: llm-anthropic 0.25 Release
description: New model support for claude-opus-4.7 with thinking_effort:xhigh feature. New thinking_display and thinking_adaptive boolean options. Increased default max_tokens to maximum allowed for each model.
author: Simon Willison

title: Factory Hits $1.5B Valuation to Build AI Coding for Enterprises
description: Factory, an AI coding startup, reached $1.5B valuation to build AI coding tools for enterprises. This shows continued massive investment in AI-powered development tools.
author: Marina Temkin

title: OpenAI Takes Aim at Anthropic with Beefed-up Codex
description: OpenAI released an enhanced Codex model that gives it more power over your desktop, directly competing with Anthropic's Claude. This shows intensifying competition in AI coding assistance.
author: Lucas Ropek

title: datasette 1.0a27 Release - CSRF Protection Changes
description: Datasette no longer uses Django-style CSRF form tokens, instead using modern browser headers (Sec-Fetch-Site) based on Filippo Valsorda's research. New RenameTableEvent for when tables are renamed during SQLite transactions.
author: Simon Willison

title: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS - Directed Text-to-Speech with Complex Prompting
description: Google released Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS, a text-to-speech model with surprisingly elaborate prompting capabilities requiring detailed character profiles, scene descriptions, and directorial notes. Simon vibe-coded a UI for trying it out.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI Announces GPT-5.4-Cyber for Defensive Security
description: OpenAI released GPT-5.4-Cyber, a cyber-permissive model fine-tuned for defensive cybersecurity use cases. They also extended their 'Trusted Access for Cyber' program requiring identity verification via Persona.
author: Simon Willison

title: Cybersecurity Looks Like Proof of Work Now
description: UK's AI Safety Institute evaluation of Claude Mythos shows that more tokens (money) spent leads to better security results. This creates economic incentive to spend more on security reviews than attackers spend exploiting. Open source libraries become more valuable as security investment can be shared.
author: Simon Willison (citing Drew Breunig)

title: Servo v0.1.0 Crate - Embeddable Browser Engine for Rust
description: Simon used Claude Code to explore the new Servo crate, building a CLI tool called 'servo-shot' for taking screenshots. Servo provides an embeddable browser engine for Rust with clear API around ServoBuilder, WebView, and pixel readback methods.
author: Simon Willison

title: The Peril of Laziness Lost - LLMs Lack Virtue of Laziness
description: Bryan Cantrill argues that LLMs inherently lack the virtue of laziness - work costs nothing to them, so they create larger, not better systems. Human laziness forces us to develop crisp abstractions to avoid wasting our time.
author: Simon Willison (citing Bryan Cantrill)

title: Audio Transcription with Gemma 4 E2B using MLX
description: Simon shared a uv run recipe for transcribing audio files on macOS using the 10.28 GB Gemma 4 E2B model with MLX and mlx-vlm. Demonstrated successful transcription of a 14-second wav file with minor accuracy issues.
author: Simon Willison
